slot.brief: Energy-level diagram of hydrogen with a few marked transitions; identify which jump emits a given spectral series photon and compute its wavelength.

stem: The marked downward transitions in hydrogen are shown in the figure. Which transition gives the first line of the Paschen series, and what is its wavelength? Take $R = 1.097\times10^7$ m$^{-1}$.

verdicts.working: The first Paschen line is the transition from n=4 to n=3, shown as C. Using 1/λ = R(1/3² − 1/4²) = 7R/144 gives λ ≈ 1.88 μm.

working:
$\text{Paschen series: } n_f=3;\quad \text{first line: } n_i=4$
$\dfrac{1}{\lambda}=R\left(\dfrac{1}{3^2}-\dfrac{1}{4^2}\right)=\dfrac{7R}{144}$
$\lambda=\dfrac{144}{7R}=1.875\times10^{-6}\ \text{m}=1.88\ \mu\text{m}$

Independent check: The first Paschen line is the transition from n=4 to n=3, shown as C. Using 1/λ = R(1/3² − 1/4²) = 7R/144 gives λ ≈ 1.88 μm.

draft.stem: The marked downward transitions in hydrogen are shown in the figure. Which transition gives the first line of the Paschen series, and what is its wavelength? Take $R = 1.097\times10^7$ m$^{-1}$.

figure.description: Draw five horizontal energy levels, with energy increasing upward. Label them from bottom to top $n=1$, $n=2$, $n=3$, $n=4$, and $n=5$. Add four downward arrows at distinct horizontal positions: arrow A from $n=5$ to $n=3$; arrow B from $n=4$ to $n=2$; arrow C from $n=4$ to $n=3$; and arrow D from $n=3$ to $n=1$. Place each arrow's letter beside it. No other labels or values.

draft.distractor_notes: A: uses the $5\to3$ transition instead of the first Paschen line; B: selects a transition ending at $n=2$; D: selects a transition ending at the ground state.
